issue_context.title: BUG: Series[int] + datetime64 should raise
issue_context.body:
identified [here](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/commit/a6c0d02c99cfaf90119d1316dd897019326472c1#r34783276).  We handle this correctly for timedelta64, but apparently not datetime64

```
iser = pd.Series(range(3))
dt = np.datetime64(3, "D")

>>> iser + dt
0   1970-01-04
1   1970-01-05
2   1970-01-06
```

Should behave like `iser + pd.Timestamp(dt)`:

```
>>> iser + pd.Timestamp(dt)
[...]
ValueError: Cannot add integral value to Timestamp without freq.
```

review_comments: can this ever be called with a ``datetime.datetime`` (or subclass eg Timestamp),?
datetime and Timestamp both behave correctly already, also are included in the test
in ensure_python_int we have a `assert new_value == value` (inside a try/except) that numpy is warning about when `value` is a np.datetime64 obj

This raises for me with NumPy 1.17

```python

In [13]: a = np.datetime64(10, 'ns')

In [14]: pd.core.dtypes.common.ensure_python_int(a)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
AssertionError                            Traceback (most recent call last)
~/sandbox/pandas/pandas/core/dtypes/common.py in ensure_python_int(value)
    203         new_value = int(value)
--> 204         assert new_value == value
    205     except (TypeError, ValueError, AssertionError):

AssertionError:

During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:

TypeError                                 Traceback (most recent call last)
<ipython-input-14-a45e0cb68b99> in <module>
----> 1 pd.core.dtypes.common.ensure_python_int(a)

~/sandbox/pandas/pandas/core/dtypes/common.py in ensure_python_int(value)
    204         assert new_value == value
    205     except (TypeError, ValueError, AssertionError):
--> 206         raise TypeError(msg.format(type(value), value))
    207     return new_value
    208

TypeError: Wrong type <class 'numpy.datetime64'> for value 1970-01-01T00:00:00.000000010
```

It just warned earlier? If so, then +1

> This raises for me with NumPy 1.17

Yah, the assertion raises on master, shouldn't be affected by this PR.  This PR makes `pd.Series([0]) + pd.Timestamp.now().to_datetime64()` raise TypeError, which doesn't happen now.
do we need a followup for @TomAugspurger point above? (merging in any event)

IIUC, there's no additional work needed.

Does someone with, say NumPy 1.14 see a warning then an error? It's not the cleanest but I'm probably OK with that. Working around that seems a bit messy.
